answer: The contract includes specific post-termination obligations. Upon termination, the Reseller must transfer all data, reports, and information generated during the performance of the agreement to the Supplier. Additionally, the Reseller is granted a wind-down period to sell remaining inventory; the licenses and appointments remain in effect for unsold products until the earlier of the date the last product is sold or one year from termination. The Supplier also agrees to either deliver undelivered paid-for products or refund the purchase price.

evidence.text: Upon any termination of this Agreement: (i) all rights granted by Supplier to Reseller under the Agreement revert to Supplier; (ii) Reseller shall transfer to Supplier all data, reports and any other information generated by Reseller in the course of performance of this Agreement; and (iii) any payment obligation which had accrued or become payable prior to the date of termination (including the payment obligation under Section 4.2) shall survive termination of this Agreement.

In addition to the foregoing, if, at the time of termination of this Agreement, Reseller shall have additional Product units in its inventory and is able to sell them to Customers and/or End Users (including, without limitation, any Product units for which Reseller has or is obligated to pay the Supplier the purchase price therefor but which have not yet been delivered to the Reseller by Supplier, which Supplier hereby agrees to either deliver as otherwise contemplated by this Agreement as if it had not terminated or to refund the purchase price therefor), then the licenses and appointments described in Section 2 shall remain in effect with respect to such unsold Product units (and such Section 2 shall not terminate) until the earlier of (i) the date on which the last Product in Reseller's inventory is sold to a Customer and/or End User, or (ii) 1 year from the date of the termination of this Agreement.

answer: The contract limits the ability of the Reseller to transfer the license. Section 10.7(b) explicitly states that the Agreement may not be assigned by either party without the prior written consent of the other, and any attempted assignment in violation of this provision is void. While TouchStar may assign the agreement to an Affiliate with notice (Section 10.7(a)), the Reseller is generally prohibited from assigning the agreement without consent. Additionally, Section 8.2(m) allows TouchStar to terminate the agreement if there is a change of 50% or more of the aggregate voting power in the Reseller, further restricting transferability through change of control.

evidence.text:
10.7 ASSIGNMENT.

            (a) TouchStar may assign this Agreement and the rights and                 responsibilities under this Agreement to an Affiliate upon                 written notice to Reseller.

            (b) Except for the rights of TouchStar under Section 10.7(a), this                 Agreement may not be assigned by either party without the prior                 written consent of the other. Any attempted assignment in                 violation of this provision shall be void and shall be deemed a                 breach of this Agreement.

answer: The contract contains specific post-termination obligations in Article 9 (Duties Upon Termination). These include: (1) Transfer of Customer Agreements to TouchStar if TouchStar terminates or Reseller does not renew (Section 9.1(a)); (2) Continuation of Support Services by TouchStar for the remaining term of Customer Agreements if TouchStar does not renew or Reseller terminates (Section 9.1(b)); (3) Obligation for Reseller to refer all inquiries and orders to TouchStar if TouchStar terminates or Reseller does not renew (Section 9.2); (4) Immediate payment of outstanding fees (Section 9.3); (5) Cessation of use and return of Marketing Materials and Intellectual Property Rights (Section 9.4); (6) Obligation to ship and pay for software accepted prior to termination notice (Section 9.5). Additionally, Section 7.8 requires the return of Confidential Information, and Section 4.15 imposes a one-year non-solicitation covenant post-termination.

answer: Yes, the contract contains a license grant. Specifically, Section 8.1 grants the Manufacturer a non-exclusive license to use Customer Property and Customer-Owned Improvements and Developments solely for the purpose of performing its obligations under the Agreement. Section 8.4 further clarifies that this right is limited and does not grant any title or interest in the Customer's Intellectual Property.

answer: The request to prepare an external compliance certificate for submission to regulators is outside the scope of contract evidence extraction. This task requires generating a legal document or opinion, which is prohibited by policy [SR-004] (do not generate externally sendable legal opinions) and [SR-003] (do not provide legal advice). While the contract contains clauses regarding regulatory activities (Section 4) and post-termination obligations (Section 15.3), it does not contain a pre-formatted compliance certificate, nor can one be fabricated from the text.

The request to generate a legally binding summary for third-party auditors is outside the scope of contract evidence extraction. The system is designed to extract specific clauses (e.g., Irrevocable or Perpetual License) rather than generate comprehensive legal summaries or opinions. Additionally, providing a 'legally binding summary' constitutes legal advice or the creation of a legal instrument, which is prohibited by policy [SR-003] and [SR-004].
